items.title: Gaussian row marginals and the simultaneous cutoff event

source.anchor: Appendix C.2 p1 independent Gaussian columns and coordinate rows; p10 Ex104/Ex105 and the printed probability at least0.999; standing 2q+1<d
source.attribution: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling, arXiv:2610.20492v1.
source.scope: Each row marginal and the all-good cutoff in the canonical realization of the source independent-column experiment. Full joint-row independence is excluded.

items.statement: Every coordinate row of the independent-column Gaussian experiment has law \(N(0,I_r)\). In this same experiment, all row squared norms are at most \(2r+3\log(1000d)\) with probability at least \(999/1000\).
assumptions: Let \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), and \(r=q+1\). Hence \(d\ge2\) and \(r\ge1\); \(q=0\) is included.

Write \(\gamma_n=N(0,I_n)\) on real \(n\)-dimensional Euclidean space. The outcome space is \(\Omega=(\mathbb R^d)^r\), with the literal product probability measure \(\mu=\gamma_d^{\otimes r}\). Its \(r\) column vectors are independent by this fixed construction.

The \(i\)-th row map is \(\Phi_i(\omega)=(\omega_{1,i},\ldots,\omega_{r,i})\in\mathbb R^r\). Lean uses \(a.val+1\) and \(i.val+1\) for the source column and row indices, respectively; WithLp.toLp supplies the Euclidean row norm.
Put \(R_i(\omega)=\|\Phi_i(\omega)\|^2\) and \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\). The good event is the simultaneous closed cutoff \(\{\forall i,\ R_i\le L\}\); each bad event uses the strict inequality \(L<R_i\).

The public conclusion MeasurePreserving includes both measurability of each row map and its exact Gaussian pushforward law. These are proved outputs. Exponential integrability, the exact exponential moment, the tail estimates and event measurability are also derived internally.

The private consumer measures the good event under this same \(\mu\), using the exact ENNReal threshold ofReal \((999/1000)\). No retained-law normalization, auxiliary law certificate, \(\tau\)-smallness or condition-number premise is added. No Gaussian assertion is made about a norm on the function carrier \(\Omega\).

obligations.label: Each marginal row law in the source column-product realization, with a real same-experiment cutoff consumer.

bindings.boundary: The public theorem proves each marginal row law in the canonical independent-column realization; the complete private consumer proves the printed simultaneous cutoff probability in that same experiment. Marginals alone do not establish joint-row independence. Transfer from an arbitrary extended ambient experiment, full joint-row independence, original matrix-expectation adapters, centered variance, concentration, Fact C.6 and full Lemma 4.4 remain open. Both main lower bounds, exact oracle/TV/precision/worst-case cap/expected-cost adapters, serialized integration, full desktop/mobile source-index/graph delivery and purification remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: Independent N(0,I_d) columns g_1,...,g_r with r=q+1 and standing 2q+1<d.
assumption_deltas.lean: The literal finite product of r canonical standard d-dimensional Gaussian measures; natural q includes0.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is the canonical realization of the specified independent-column experiment. No transfer to every possible extended ambient probability space is claimed.

assumption_deltas.source: The coordinate rows gamma_i=(g_1i,...,g_ri) have N(0,I_r) law; p1 also asserts their joint independence.
assumption_deltas.lean: Every literal coordinate-row map is MeasurePreserving to the canonical row Gaussian.
assumption_deltas.reason: This binding covers the marginal-law subclaim only. Both measurability and map_eq are outputs. The stronger source joint-row independence claim remains outside this local obligation.

assumption_deltas.source: p10 states probability at least0.999 for the all-row closed cutoff L=2r+3log(1000d).
assumption_deltas.lean: The complete private consumer proves ofReal(999/1000)<=mu good in that same fixed product experiment.
assumption_deltas.reason: Exponential integrability, exact moment transport, strict tails, finite union and good-event measurability are proved internally. The union-bound expansion is explicitly an inference supporting the printed source probability.
